name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Monday 12 December 1983

clue.text: Called to mind a wager about admitting . . .

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps itself around the next

blocks.note: a bet is a wager
though can mean admitting that, as in conceding a point

explanation.surface: Remembering a bet that involved some confession, continued into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots link this to 2 down only for the surface. 'Admitting' is the inserted word here, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bethought is the past tense of bethink, an old verb meaning to remember or consider.

clue.text: . . . I'm on the left; to the worker that's significant

blocks.note: taken as written
port is the left side of a ship
a worker ant, the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A left-wing confession that labour matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' sounds political but is the nautical side, port.
explanation.definitionFit: Something important carries weight or meaning, a direct synonym for significant.

clue.text: Rent to the Navy

blocks.note: taken as written
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Paying housing costs to the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid for housing, but it is the past participle of rend, to tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent, as a past participle of rend, means ripped apart, just as torn does.

clue.text: Indecorous state to find guide in!

indicators.note: to be in a state is to be agitated and disordered, so the letters that follow are jumbled

blocks.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a scandalous region where one must look for a tour leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a region or nation, but it signals the letters are in a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Undignified behaviour lacks propriety and decorum, which is what indecorous describes.

clue.text: Antonio Napoli - part Spanish, perhaps . . .

indicators.note: only a part of the named person's words is wanted, a run of letters within them

blocks.note: the letters span the end of the first name and the start of the surname

explanation.surface: A man from Naples of partly Spanish descent, the thought trailing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Spanish' as nationality; it is a variety of vegetable, flagged by 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish onion is a large mild variety, so Spanish is one example of the bulb.

clue.text: like myself – and one native

blocks.note: 'as I' means like me, the setter speaking
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: Continuing 5 down: someone partly foreign like the speaker, and also a local.
explanation.definitionFit: An Asian is a person born in Asia, one example of a native of a place.

clue.text: Sides of a stem

blocks.note: the five letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A botanist describing the two flanks of a plant's stalk.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'a stem' rearrange to TEAMS; the printed clue has no word signalling the rearrangement, so the solver has to spot it unaided.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport the opposing sides in a match are the two competing teams.

clue.text: Healthy condition in the strait, put on a cape

blocks.note: a sound is a narrow stretch of sea between two land masses
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour place names

explanation.surface: A seafarer's wellbeing while sailing a channel and rounding a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUND and NESS are both geographical words, which the surface's seafaring picture hides in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Soundness is the state of being in good health, as in soundness of body and mind.

clue.text: New growth out of fire?

blocks.note: first meaning: a young stem sprouting from a plant
second meaning: to discharge a gun

explanation.surface: Fresh green sprouts appearing after a bushfire.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests regrowth after a blaze, but 'fire' is a verb meaning to discharge a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a young plant sprout and the act of discharging a gun.

clue.text: Backward boy makes short work of it, going to North America on the other side of the world

definitions.text: on the other side of the world

indicators.note: something backward faces the wrong way, so the whole string built here is read from end to start

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
op. is the short form of opus, a musical work
'it' taken as written, with 'of' joining
NA is the abbreviation for North America

explanation.surface: A dawdling lad dashes through a job before heading off to America on the far side of the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' looks like it describes the boy, but it applies to the whole chain of pieces, which is then read in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipodal places lie diametrically opposite each other on the globe, as Australia is to Britain.

clue.text: Hibernation buries student outcry

blocks.note: to inter is to bury
L is the learner plate, standing for a student
a weep is a cry of grief

explanation.surface: A dormant spell that smothers a student protest.
explanation.walkthrough: No word signals the placing, so the solver must split WEEP after its first letter to hold the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibernation is the deep dormancy animals pass through in the cold season.

clue.text: A few well-chosen words would put an end to the scene

definitions.text: A few well-chosen words would put an end to the scene

blocks.clueFragment: A few well-chosen words would put an end to the scene
blocks.note: surface reading: a tactful remark that defuses a quarrel or public fuss

blocks.clueFragment: put an end to the scene
blocks.note: setter's reading: in a theatre, a scene literally ends with a final spoken line before the drop comes down

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scene' suggests a row or embarrassing fuss; here it is a scene in a play, closed by its last line.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre this is the closing speech of a scene or act, delivered just before the stage drape falls.

clue.text: Not telling the truth. Heather, about youth leader

indicators.note: a leader goes at the front, so only the opening letter is taken
about means around, so the plant word is wrapped around the selected letter

blocks.note: ling is common heather
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Accusing someone called Heather of fibbing about a youth leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name, but it is the moorland plant, ling.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying means telling falsehoods, the opposite of telling the truth.

clue.text: A writer with cunning I have admitted thoughtfully

indicators.note: something admitted is let inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: a pen is a writing instrument
sly means cunning
the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A crafty author owning up to something after reflection.
explanation.definitionFit: Pensively means in a deeply reflective way, an adverb like thoughtfully.

clue.text: Wayfarer shows how all revert

indicators.note: showing how a thing could be made demonstrates another arrangement of its letters

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wanderer demonstrating that everyone eventually goes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revert' tempts a reading-backwards approach, but it is part of the letters to be mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A wayfarer is someone journeying on foot, a direct synonym for a traveller.

clue.text: Avoid going in as hunters do

indicators.note: the answer goes inside the following words, sitting within their run of letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A hunter's tactic of steering clear of entering cover.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun something is to keep away from it deliberately, a synonym for avoid.

clue.text: Taker may be wrong if he . . .

definitions.text: Taker may be wrong if he

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of their correct order and need putting right

blocks.note: the opening letter of the first word
the four letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that whoever takes something may be in the wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots lead into 18 across. No word signals that only the first letter of 'Taker' is used, so this is a loose all-in-one clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief is someone who takes what is not theirs, so the whole clue describes one.

clue.text: . . . drum container gets left in the count

blocks.note: the eardrum is housed inside the ear
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A drum's case is left behind at a tally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drum' is the eardrum, not a musical instrument; 'count' is a nobleman, not a tally.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is the British rank equivalent to a continental count.

clue.text: Advancing by stages, get on with 4 at the Point

blocks.note: to progress is to get on or move forward
IV is four in Roman numerals
E (east) is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Instructions for moving forward step by step toward a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: The '4' looks like a pointer to 4 down but is simply the number, written as a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Something progressive proceeds step by step, increasing gradually in stages.

clue.text: Dr Hill is a mover.. .

blocks.note: an MO is a medical officer, a doctor
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: A doctor named Hill described as a go-getter.
explanation.walkthrough: Hill looks like a surname for the doctor; it is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor is the engine that makes a machine move, so it is a mover.

clue.text: . . . but Stella Knight is stiff

blocks.note: stella is Latin for star
K is the abbreviation for knight, as in KBE or KG

explanation.surface: Continuing 20 down: a woman named Stella Knight is rigid, unlike the lively doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Stella Knight reads as a person's name; the first name is Latin for a celestial body.
explanation.definitionFit: Stark can mean rigid, as a corpse lying stark and stiff.

clue.text: Take for granted, if mail is delayed, that superior will intervene

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so one piece is set in the middle of the others

blocks.note: post is mail
delayed means late
U stands for upper-class, hence superior

explanation.surface: Assume your boss will step in if the post runs behind.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old British label for upper-class usage, so it stands for superior.
explanation.definitionFit: To postulate is to assume something as a basis for reasoning without proof.

clue.text: At the Turk's Head regret being faithful

indicators.note: a head is the top or front, so only the opening letter of the word is used

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Remorse felt at a pub called the Turk's Head about loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The Turk's Head sounds like an inn sign; the Head is the first letter of the word Turk's.
explanation.definitionFit: True means loyal and steadfast, as in a true friend, so it fits faithful.

clue.text: Sins and lives disgracefully

indicators.note: behaving disgracefully means acting badly, so the following word's letters are thrown out of their proper order

blocks.note: the five letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who transgresses and leads a shameful existence.
explanation.definitionFit: Evils are wicked deeds, the plural noun matching sins.

clue.text: Set course out to be obliging

indicators.note: to set something is to arrange it, so the words after it are put into a fresh order

blocks.note: the nine letters of both words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A navigator charting a route in order to be helpful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set course' reads as a navigating phrase, but 'Set' is the signal and 'out' belongs to the letters being mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A courteous person is polite and willing to help, which is what obliging means.

clue.text: Change in church? I say!

indicators.note: saying something means speaking it, so the sound of the word matters, not its spelling

blocks.note: the altar is the table at the front of a church

explanation.surface: A surprised exclamation at some reform in the church.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something is to modify or change it.
